newsitem.title: UK: Chernobyl may live into new millennium - report.
newsitem.headline: Chernobyl may live into new millennium - report.

text.p: Ukraine has threatened to keep open Chernobyl, site of the world's worst nuclear disaster, beyong the year 2000 if promised funding of $1.2 billion for two new atomic reactors is cancelled, the Financial Times reported on Thursday.

Ukraine's Environment Minister Yuri Kostenko was responding to the possibility that the European Bank of Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) may cancel payment of $400 million for the new stations on the grounds that the project was uneconomic.
The EBRD has not made a decision on the report they commissioned from an independent panel of experts, who said the project would "not represent the most productive use" of European Union funds.
The report suggested that instead of funding the project, grants as opposed to loans should be made available for other economically attractive projects in Ukraine.
Kostenko said Ukraine wants the money by July to complete work on the two reactors. Work on the reactors was suspended in 1991, five years after the Chernobyl explosion and fire.
